headline: Uncle Joe turns seventy
summary: Roosevelt spends the day lobbying a long line of senators on the rate bill and lunches with Albert Shaw. In the evening he joins the crowd at the Arlington Hotel celebrating Uncle Joe Cannon's seventieth. He assures Hannah Schoff, who leads the national mothers' congress, that Mormons have given up polygamy.

headline: Colonel Mosby calls
summary: The Cabinet discusses the California disaster and Secretary Metcalf's trip west. Roosevelt meets Kansas Attorney General Davidson on the Standard Oil cases, receives the old Confederate raider John Mosby, and lunches with James Speyer.

headline: H. G. Wells comes to lunch
summary: Roosevelt meets Upton Sinclair in the morning and lunches with H. G. Wells, then touring America for a newspaper series. The two disagree, but Roosevelt tells Wells that even if nations must decline, he chooses to live as if America will not, and that the effort is worth it.

tr_quotes.text: Suppose, after all, that should prove to be right, and it all ends in your butterflies and morlocks. That doesn't matter now. The effort's real. It's worth going on with. It's worth it. It's worth it - even so.

headline: Permission to punish Quentin
